Button

An action the reader takes on the current view.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • To start, save, confirm or cancel something on the current view.
  • To submit a form.

When not to use it

  • To go to another view or another site. Use a link.
  • For an action repeated on every row of a list. Give that one secondary or quiet emphasis, never primary.
  • As a second primary action in the same view. A view has one.

Variants

secondary
The default, with no modifier class. Any action that is not the main one. A tonal fill a step from the page and from a raised card, with a faint border that turns strong on hover; unavailable, it loses the fill.
primary ds-button--primary
The one main action of a view, dialog or popover.
quiet ds-button--quiet
A minor action that should not draw the eye, such as Cancel or View log.
danger ds-button--danger
An action that deletes or cannot be undone. The label names what is lost.

Sizes

default
44px tall. Use it unless the button sits in a dense row.
small ds-button--small
Drawn 32px tall for dense rows and toolbars. Its pointer target is still 44px.

Accessibility

  • Use a button element, with type="button" unless it submits a form.
  • The label is a verb and what it acts on, such as Start task. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
  • Set the disabled attribute when the action is unavailable. A disabled button leaves the tab order.
  • Use aria-disabled="true" instead only when the button must stay focusable so its reason can be read. The app then ignores presses.
  • Set aria-busy="true" while the action runs, change the label to say what is happening, and ignore further presses.
  • Enter and Space activate it. Both come from the button element.

Classes

  • ds-button
  • ds-button--danger
